description.text: The promos of the Black & White Series, numbered BW01 to BW101 and released from March 2011 to December 2013, when the prefix changed from HGSS to BW. Most came in products: blisters of each expansion, tins, boxes and collections. Some went to players, from prerelease events, which also gave staff copies, to the World Championships trophy cards Tropical Beach (2011 and 2012) and Champions Festival (2013); the Supporter N, BW100, was a Pokémon League prize. Keldeo and Genesect came with DVD releases of their films. Two numbers were never released: Pikachu BW77 and Raichu BW78 were meant for the Plasma Freeze three-pack blisters of May 2013, but after a planned English Landorus Box was cancelled, Landorus BW79 and Druddigon BW80 went into the blisters instead. Pokémon.com showed the two cards for one night in July 2014, and they could be played in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online, but no printed copy was ever sold.

tell.text: A black star promo symbol and a "BW" number at the bottom right

description.text:
A holofoil Snivy from the Sneak-Peek Tins of March 2011, which brought the first Unova Pokémon to the English card game a month before the Black & White set. Each tin held Snivy, Tepig BW02 or Oshawott BW03 with a figure of the same Pokémon, four older booster packs and a preview pack of five cards from the coming Black & White set. These three were the first Black & White promos.

Ken Sugimori's drawing first came in Japan in September 2010 in the Journey Partners collection, with Snivy standing in front of a house; the English card puts it on a new swirling background. Japan reprinted its own version several times, last as a prize of JR Hokkaido's Pokémon Battle Train in August 2011, for finishing the Reshiram Route on the games' Battle Subway. The English art came back in 2021 with the 25th anniversary logo, in McDonald's collection that year and as a jumbo card in the Unova First Partner Pack.

A holofoil Tepig from the Sneak-Peek Tins of March 2011, which brought the first Unova Pokémon to the English card game a month before the Black & White set. Each tin held Snivy BW01, Tepig or Oshawott BW03 with a figure of the same Pokémon, four older booster packs and a preview pack of five cards from the coming Black & White set. These three were the first Black & White promos.

Ken Sugimori's drawing first came in Japan in September 2010 in the Journey Partners collection, with Tepig in front of a house; the English card puts it on a new burst of light. Japan reprinted its own version several times, last as a prize of JR Hokkaido's Pokémon Battle Train in summer 2011, for finishing the Victini Route on the games' Battle Subway. The English art came back in 2021 with the 25th anniversary logo, in McDonald's collection that year and as a jumbo card in the Unova First Partner Pack.

A holofoil Oshawott from the Sneak-Peek Tins of March 2011, which brought the first Unova Pokémon to the English card game a month before the Black & White set. Each tin held Snivy BW01, Tepig BW02 or Oshawott with a figure of the same Pokémon, four older booster packs and a preview pack of five cards from the coming Black & White set. These three were the first Black & White promos.

Ken Sugimori's drawing first came in Japan in September 2010 in the Journey Partners collection, with Oshawott beside a white fence; the English card puts it on a new burst of light. Japan reprinted its own version several times, last as a prize of JR Hokkaido's Pokémon Battle Train in August 2011, for finishing the Zekrom Route on the games' Battle Subway. The English art came back in 2021 with the 25th anniversary logo, in McDonald's collection that year and as a jumbo card in the Unova First Partner Pack.

A holofoil Reshiram from one of the two New Legends Tins of spring 2011, each with four Black & White booster packs; the other held Zekrom BW005. The two carry three-digit numbers, BW004 and BW005, where the promos around them have two. Later shipments of the tins, sold at stores such as Walgreens, held three packs from newer sets instead.

It reprints the Black & White set's Reshiram (number 26) with art made only for English: 5ban Graphics turned the same 3D model to a new angle. Reshiram came back as a promo later in 2011 with other art, as BW23 in the Reshiram Box.

A holofoil Zekrom from one of the two New Legends Tins of spring 2011, each with four Black & White booster packs; the other held Reshiram BW004. The two carry three-digit numbers, BW004 and BW005, where the promos around them have two. Later shipments of the tins, sold at stores such as Walgreens, held three packs from newer sets instead.

It reprints the Black & White set's Zekrom (number 47) with art made only for English: 5ban Graphics turned the same 3D model to a new angle. Zekrom came back as a promo later in 2011 with other art, as BW24 in the Zekrom Box.

A holofoil Snivy from the Black & White blisters of April 2011, released with the Black & White set. The three-pack blister held three booster packs, a sampling pack of three common cards and a coin showing the Unova first partners, with Snivy, Tepig BW07 or Oshawott BW08; the two-pack blister held one booster pack and a sampling pack with one of the same three or Ducklett BW17.

Shizurow's art first came in Japan as Snivy 018/BW-P, one of six cards, five Pokémon and a Pokédex, given with Pokémon T-shirts from the clothing brand Uniqlo from 14 March 2011. The other Uniqlo Pokémon became Tepig BW07, Oshawott BW08, Zorua BW12 and Minccino BW13.

A holofoil Tepig from the Black & White blisters of April 2011, released with the Black & White set. The three-pack blister held three booster packs, a sampling pack of three common cards and a coin showing the Unova first partners, with Snivy BW06, Tepig or Oshawott BW08; the two-pack blister held one booster pack and a sampling pack with one of the same three or Ducklett BW17.

Shin Nagasawa's art first came in Japan as Tepig 019/BW-P, one of six cards, five Pokémon and a Pokédex, given with Pokémon T-shirts from the clothing brand Uniqlo from 14 March 2011. The other Uniqlo Pokémon became Snivy BW06, Oshawott BW08, Zorua BW12 and Minccino BW13.

A holofoil Oshawott from the Black & White blisters of April 2011, released with the Black & White set. The three-pack blister held three booster packs, a sampling pack of three common cards and a coin showing the Unova first partners, with Snivy BW06, Tepig BW07 or Oshawott; the two-pack blister held one booster pack and a sampling pack with one of the same three or Ducklett BW17.

Mitsuhiro Arita's art first came in Japan as Oshawott 020/BW-P, one of six cards, five Pokémon and a Pokédex, given with Pokémon T-shirts from the clothing brand Uniqlo from 14 March 2011. The other Uniqlo Pokémon became Snivy BW06, Tepig BW07, Zorua BW12 and Minccino BW13.

A holofoil Zoroark from the Victini Box, released with the Black & White set in April 2011 with a Victini figure on a stand and five Black & White booster packs.

It reprints the Black & White set's Zoroark (number 71) with a new drawing by the same artist, Naoki Saito. In Japan this art was Zoroark 007/BW-P, given to players who bought a booster box of the Black Collection or White Collection, Japan's first Black & White sets, from a store hosting Gym Challenge tournaments. The Japanese print carries the two sets' logos, which the English one drops.

A holofoil Axew from the Black & White Collector's Album Box of April 2011, which held a mini album for 60 cards and two Black & White booster packs.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan in December 2010 as Axew 003/BW-P, from a promotion celebrating the Egg Ash received in the anime: buying Black Collection or White Collection booster packs earned one of three cards, Pansage, Pidove or Axew. 7-Eleven stores gave out versions with different art, which America got later in April 2011 in the Toys "R" Us booster two-packs, Axew among them as BW16. The Japanese print carries the two sets' logos, which the English one drops.

A holofoil Pansage from the Emerging Powers three-pack blister of August 2011, with Emerging Powers booster packs and a coin showing Reshiram and Zekrom. The other three-pack blister held Zorua BW12.

Akira Komayama's art first came in Japan in December 2010 as Pansage 001/BW-P, from the promotion celebrating the Egg Ash received in the anime: buying Black Collection or White Collection booster packs earned Pansage, Pidove or Axew. 7-Eleven stores gave out a version with different art, which America got first, in April 2011, as Pansage BW14.

A holofoil Zorua from the Emerging Powers three-pack blister of August 2011, with Emerging Powers booster packs and a coin showing Reshiram and Zekrom. The other three-pack blister held Pansage BW11.

Tomokazu Komiya's art first came in Japan as Zorua 021/BW-P, one of six cards given with Pokémon T-shirts from the clothing brand Uniqlo from 14 March 2011. Snivy, Tepig and Oshawott from the same campaign came to English first, as BW06-BW08 in the Black & White blisters; Zorua and Minccino BW13 followed with Emerging Powers.

A Minccino from the Emerging Powers two-pack blister of August 2011, with one Emerging Powers booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The card came in two foils, cosmos holo or cracked ice holo.

Atsuko Nishida's art first came in Japan as Minccino 022/BW-P, one of six cards given with Pokémon T-shirts from the clothing brand Uniqlo from 14 March 2011. Snivy, Tepig and Oshawott from the same campaign came to English first, as BW06-BW08 in the Black & White blisters; Minccino and Zorua BW12 followed with Emerging Powers.

description.text:
A Pansage from the Black & White booster two-packs that Toys "R" Us sold from 27 April 2011, each with two Black & White booster packs and one of three promos, Pansage, Pidove BW15 or Axew BW16, hidden behind a card showing their silhouettes. The packs went with the store's Secret Egg promotion, in which players downloaded an Egg to Pokémon Black or White that hatched into one of the same three: Cilan's Pansage, Ash's Pidove or Iris's Axew from the anime.

Akira Komayama's art first came in Japan in December 2010 as Pansage 004/BW-P, given out at 7-Eleven stores in the promotion celebrating the Egg Ash received in the anime; other stores gave out a version with different art, which became Pansage BW11. From February 2013 Japan reprinted this art as 202/BW-P, with the Pokémon Pan logo, in packs of Daiichi Pan's melon and curry bread.

A Pidove from the Black & White booster two-packs that Toys "R" Us sold from 27 April 2011, each with two Black & White booster packs and one of three promos, Pansage BW14, Pidove or Axew BW16, hidden behind a card showing their silhouettes. The packs went with the store's Secret Egg promotion, in which players downloaded an Egg to Pokémon Black or White that hatched into one of the same three: Cilan's Pansage, Ash's Pidove or Iris's Axew from the anime.

Naoki Saito's art first came in Japan in December 2010 as Pidove 005/BW-P, given out at 7-Eleven stores in the promotion celebrating the Egg Ash received in the anime; other stores gave out 002/BW-P, a different drawing of Pidove in flight. From February 2013 Japan reprinted this art as 205/BW-P, with the Pokémon Pan logo, in packs of Daiichi Pan's melon and curry bread.

An Axew from the Black & White booster two-packs that Toys "R" Us sold from 27 April 2011, each with two Black & White booster packs and one of three promos, Pansage BW14, Pidove BW15 or Axew, hidden behind a card showing their silhouettes. The packs went with the store's Secret Egg promotion, in which players downloaded an Egg to Pokémon Black or White that hatched into one of the same three: Cilan's Pansage, Ash's Pidove or Iris's Axew from the anime.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan in December 2010 as Axew 006/BW-P, given out at 7-Eleven stores in the promotion celebrating the Egg Ash received in the anime; other stores gave out a version with different art, which became Axew BW10. From February 2013 Japan reprinted this art as 206/BW-P, with the Pokémon Pan logo, in packs of Daiichi Pan's melon and curry bread.

A holofoil Ducklett from the Black & White two-pack blister of 2011, with one Black & White booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The same blister also came with Snivy BW06, Tepig BW07 or Oshawott BW08, but Ducklett came only in this one, at stores such as Target and Wal-Mart.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan as Ducklett 008/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's February 2011 Gym Challenge tournaments; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo. It redraws the Black & White set's Ducklett (number 36), also by Himeno.

A holofoil Darumaka from the Emerging Powers Collector's Album Box, released with Emerging Powers on 31 August 2011 with a mini album for 60 cards and two Emerging Powers booster packs.

Akira Komayama's art first came in Japan as Darumaka 048/BW-P, from a campaign at the pizza chain Pizza-La that began on 29 April 2011: with a pizza, customers could buy a starter deck, a deck box and three promos, Darumaka, Scraggy and Axew, which came to English as BW18, BW25 and BW26. All three drawings are full of Berries from the games; Darumaka carries a basket of them on its head.

A holofoil Zoroark from the Zoroark-Illusions Collection of October 2011, a box with this card, a jumbo 3D copy of it, three booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

The art first came in Japan as Zoroark 024/BW-P at the Next Generation World Hobby Fair of January 2011. Its attacks, Punishment and Snarl, are the moves of the event Zoroark given out at the same fair; at the time no other Pokémon in the games could know Snarl. In America, Toys "R" Us gave out a Zoroark with Snarl from 18 to 25 September 2011, shortly before the box came out.

The picture moves or changes as the card tilts, under a ridged plastic face. An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.

description.text: The jumbo copy is a 3D card from the same box: printed on thick lenticular plastic, with Darkness Energy symbols tiled in the background that seem to stand out in 3D.

A holofoil Serperior from the Evolved Battle Action Tins of 2011, each with Serperior, Emboar BW21 or Samurott BW22, a figure of the same Pokémon, five booster packs (usually two Emerging Powers and one each of Black & White, Call of Legends and Triumphant) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Later shipments, sold at stores such as Walgreens, left out the figure and held three newer packs.

It reprints the holofoil Serperior of the Black & White set (number 6), with its Royal Heal Ability, in art 5ban Graphics made only for English.

A holofoil Emboar from the Evolved Battle Action Tins of 2011, each with Serperior BW20, Emboar or Samurott BW22, a figure of the same Pokémon, five booster packs (usually two Emerging Powers and one each of Black & White, Call of Legends and Triumphant) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Later shipments, sold at stores such as Walgreens, left out the figure and held three newer packs.

It reprints the holofoil Emboar of the Black & White set (number 20), with its Inferno Fandango Ability, in art 5ban Graphics made only for English.

A holofoil Samurott from the Evolved Battle Action Tins of 2011, each with Serperior BW20, Emboar BW21 or Samurott, a figure of the same Pokémon, five booster packs (usually two Emerging Powers and one each of Black & White, Call of Legends and Triumphant) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Later shipments, sold at stores such as Walgreens, left out the figure and held three newer packs.

It reprints the holofoil Samurott of the Black & White set (number 32), with its Shell Armor Ability, in art 5ban Graphics made only for English.

A holofoil Reshiram from the Reshiram Box of October 2011, with a large Reshiram figure, four booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The Zekrom Box held Zekrom BW24.

It reprints the Black & White set's Reshiram (number 26) with 5ban Graphics' art from the English Black & White booster packs. Japan had released the same card in July 2011 as Reshiram 051/BW-P, in the Reshiram Special Trunk Set, a trunk for storing cards with six booster packs.

A holofoil Zekrom from the Zekrom Box of October 2011, with a Zekrom figure on a stand, four booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The Reshiram Box held Reshiram BW23.

It reprints the Black & White set's Zekrom (number 47) with 5ban Graphics' art from the English Black & White booster packs. Japan had released the same card in July 2011 as Zekrom 052/BW-P, in the Zekrom Special Trunk Set, a trunk for storing cards with six booster packs.

A Scraggy from the small Noble Victories blister of late 2011, with one Noble Victories booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The card came in two foils, cosmos holo or cracked ice holo.

Akira Komayama's art first came in Japan as Scraggy 049/BW-P, the holofoil one of three promos in a campaign at the pizza chain Pizza-La from 29 April 2011, with Darumaka (English BW18) and Axew (BW26): with a pizza, customers could buy the three cards, a deck box showing them and a starter deck. Like the other two, the drawing is full of Berries from the games.

description.text:
A holofoil Axew from the Noble Victories three-pack blister of November 2011, with three Noble Victories booster packs, a sampling pack of three common cards and a Victini coin. The other three-pack blister held Litwick BW27.

Akira Komayama's art first came in Japan as Axew 050/BW-P, one of three promos in a campaign at the pizza chain Pizza-La from 29 April 2011, with Darumaka (English BW18) and Scraggy (BW25): with a pizza, customers could buy the three cards, a deck box showing them and a starter deck. Like the other two, the drawing is full of Berries from the games.

A holofoil Litwick from the Noble Victories three-pack blister of November 2011, with three Noble Victories booster packs, a sampling pack of three common cards and a Victini coin. The other three-pack blister held Axew BW26.

Atsuko Nishida's art first came in Japan as Litwick 009/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's February 2011 Gym Challenge tournaments, like Ducklett BW17; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo, which the English one drops.

Tropical Beach was the promo card of the 2011 Pokémon World Championships, held from 12 to 14 August 2011 at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront. Competitors received the card in seven languages and staff got a Staff copy. The trophy versions carry a placement stamp from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist, which was still the highest stamp: Champion copies only began the following year.

tell.text: "FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"QUARTER-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"SEMI-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"STAFF" printed on the card, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: for the people who ran the event.

description.text: The stamped staff copy, given to those who helped run the 2011 World Championships. Other stamped copies went to the top players in each division.

tell.text: "TOP SIXTEEN" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"TOP THIRTY-TWO" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
A World Championships stamp on the picture: "Worlds" and the year on early cards, the World Championships logo and year on later ones.

description.text: The 2011 Tropical Beach, given to every player of the trading card game at the start of the 2011 World Championships, in a nine-card collection: the card in seven languages and two cards announcing the date and venue of the next World Championships.

Victory Cup was the trophy card of Battle Road tournaments from Autumn 2011 to Spring 2013. This print was the prize for third place, and each copy carries the stamp of the season it was won in: Autumn 2011, Spring 2012, Autumn 2012 or Spring 2013. Separate prints went to the first-, second- and third-placed players.

Victory Cup was the trophy card of Battle Road tournaments from Autumn 2011 to Spring 2013. This print was the prize for second place, and each copy carries the stamp of the season it was won in: Autumn 2011, Spring 2012, Autumn 2012 or Spring 2013. Separate prints went to the first-, second- and third-placed players.

Victory Cup was the trophy card of Battle Road tournaments from Autumn 2011 to Spring 2013. This print was the prize for first place, and each copy carries the stamp of the season it was won in: Autumn 2011, Spring 2012, Autumn 2012 or Spring 2013. Separate prints went to the first-, second- and third-placed players. One player on Elite Fourum recalls winning a 1st Place copy at an Autumn 2011 Battle Road whose top cut was just four players.

A holofoil Victini from the V for Victini Tin of December 2011, with a Victini figure first sold in the Victini Box, five Noble Victories booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

It reprints Noble Victories' Victini (number 14) with new art by 5ban Graphics, first printed in Japan as Victini 109/BW-P in the Battle Gift Set: Thundurus vs Tornadus, a box of two ready-made decks released in November 2011. The card's Ability, Victory Star, lets the player flip an attack's coins again, which earned it the nickname Fliptini. The same card also came in promotional boxes in Italy, Germany and France.

A Riolu from 2012 blister packs, in two versions. The cosmos holofoil copy came in the Next Destinies three-pack blister of February 2012, with three Next Destinies booster packs and a coin; the other blister of that kind held Luxio BW34. That blister was sold outside North America, where the blisters held other cards. North America got Riolu in May 2012 instead, as a non-holo card in a Dark Explorers blister with a holofoil Lucario from Next Destinies, one Dark Explorers booster pack and a sampling pack of three cards.

sui's art, set in Castelia City, first came in Japan in 2011 as Riolu 104/BW-P: stores gave it, Luxio (English BW34) or Meowth (BW35) at random to customers buying five booster packs of Psycho Drive or Hail Blizzard, and the Japanese print carries those sets' logos on the art.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

description.text:
A Luxio from 2012 blister packs, in two foils. The cosmos holofoil copy came in the Next Destinies three-pack blister of February 2012, with three Next Destinies booster packs and a coin; the other blister of that kind held Riolu BW33. That blister was sold outside North America. North America got Luxio in May 2012 instead, as a cracked ice holofoil in a Dark Explorers blister with cracked ice copies of Shinx and Luxray from Next Destinies, two Dark Explorers booster packs and a coin.

Naoki Saito's art first came in Japan in 2011 as Luxio 103/BW-P: stores gave it, Riolu (English BW33) or Meowth (BW35) at random to customers buying five booster packs of Psycho Drive or Hail Blizzard, and the Japanese print carries those sets' logos on the art.

description.text:
A Meowth from a Dark Explorers blister sold in North America from May 2012, with a holofoil Persian from Next Destinies, one Dark Explorers booster pack and a sampling pack of three cards. The other blister of that kind held Riolu BW33 and Lucario.

Sumiyoshi Kizuki's art, set in Castelia City, first came in Japan in 2011 as Meowth 105/BW-P: stores gave it, Luxio (English BW34) or Riolu (BW33) at random to customers buying five booster packs of Psycho Drive or Hail Blizzard, with those sets' logos on the art. Japan reprinted it in February 2013 as 204/BW-P, one of five promos in special packs of Daiichi Pan's melon and curry breads, with the Pokémon Pan logo on the art.

A Reshiram-EX from the EX Tins of March 2012, each with Reshiram-EX, Kyurem-EX BW37 or Zekrom-EX BW38, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Unlike the tin promos of the years before, the three were neither exclusive nor drawn anew: apart from the number, each is the card from the Next Destinies set of February 2012.

Shizurow's art first came in Japan in October 2011, in the Reshiram-EX Battle Strength Deck.

A Kyurem-EX from the EX Tins of March 2012, each with Reshiram-EX BW36, Kyurem-EX or Zekrom-EX BW38, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Unlike the tin promos of the years before, the three were neither exclusive nor drawn anew: apart from the number, each is the card from the Next Destinies set of February 2012.

Shizurow's art first came in Japan in September 2011 in the Hail Blizzard set, which gave its name to the card's second attack.

A Zekrom-EX from the EX Tins of March 2012, each with Reshiram-EX BW36, Kyurem-EX BW37 or Zekrom-EX, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Unlike the tin promos of the years before, the three were neither exclusive nor drawn anew: apart from the number, each is the card from the Next Destinies set of February 2012.

Shizurow's art first came in Japan in October 2011, in the Zekrom-EX Battle Strength Deck.

A reverse holofoil Battle City from the Mewtwo Collection, released with Next Destinies on 8 February 2012: a jumbo Mewtwo-EX card, this card, a Mewtwo figure on a stand, three Next Destinies booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Hideaki Hakozaki's art of Mewtwo and Kyurem first came in Japan in 2011 as Battle City 107/BW-P, given with CoroCoro magazine to promote the Psycho Drive and Hail Blizzard sets; the Japanese print carries their logos and CoroCoro's dragon mascot. Like the Pokémon-EX of those sets, its art runs past the frame. Its effect, a coin flip each turn to draw a card, is that of the older Lucky Stadium.

Volcarona was the prerelease card of Dark Explorers, given with a deck box showing Darkrai at the set's prerelease tournaments on the weekends of 28 April and 5 May 2012, and it carries the Dark Explorers logo on the art. It was the first prerelease card to be a Black Star Promo rather than a card of the set: the set has its own Volcarona with other art.

Shin Nagasawa's art first came in Japan as Volcarona 119/BW-P, given to customers who bought a booster box of Dark Rush, the Japanese set behind Dark Explorers; the Japanese print carries the Dark Rush logo. Staff at the prereleases got copies with STAFF printed on the art.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed in the corner of the art, for the staff of the Dark Explorers prerelease tournaments.

A reverse holofoil Thundurus from the Forces of Nature Collection of April 2012, with Tornadus BW42, a full art Landorus BW43 and three booster packs.

It reprints Emerging Powers' Thundurus (number 35) with new art by 5ban Graphics, first printed in Japan in the Thundurus half of the Battle Gift Set: Thundurus vs Tornadus, a box of two ready-made decks released in November 2011.

A reverse holofoil Tornadus from the Forces of Nature Collection of April 2012, with Thundurus BW41, a full art Landorus BW43 and three booster packs.

It reprints Emerging Powers' Tornadus (number 89) with new art by 5ban Graphics, first printed in Japan in the Tornadus half of the Battle Gift Set: Thundurus vs Tornadus, a box of two ready-made decks released in November 2011.

A full art Landorus from the Forces of Nature Collection of April 2012, with reverse holofoil Thundurus BW41 and Tornadus BW42 and three booster packs.

It reprints Noble Victories' Landorus (number 74) as a full art card by 5ban Graphics, first printed in Japan as Landorus 112/BW-P in the Battle Gift Set: Thundurus vs Tornadus, a box of two ready-made decks released in November 2011. It gave Landorus a full art card like those Thundurus and Tornadus already had.

A holofoil Kyurem from the Kyurem Box of June 2012, with a Kyurem figure, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. It followed the Reshiram and Zekrom Boxes of October 2011 (BW23 and BW24), completing a box for each of the three legendary dragons of Unova.

It reprints Noble Victories' Kyurem (number 34) with English-only art by 5ban Graphics, first used on a Noble Victories booster pack.

A Mewtwo-EX from the Legendary EX Tins of 2012, out in some countries in August and in North America in September. Each tin held Mewtwo-EX, Darkrai-EX BW46 or Rayquaza-EX BW47, all three with new art, and four booster packs (usually two Dragons Exalted, one Emerging Powers and one Black & White) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Toyste Beach's art came to Japan in spring 2013: as an unnumbered promo for the top three players of each league in the World Challenge Tournament of Battle Carnival 2013 Spring, and with slightly altered art as a jumbo card in the BEAMS × Pokémon campaign that began on 20 April 2013, given to shoppers at BEAMS stores while stocks lasted.

A Darkrai-EX from the Legendary EX Tins of 2012, out in some countries in August and in North America in September. Each tin held Mewtwo-EX BW45, Darkrai-EX or Rayquaza-EX BW47, all three with new art, and four booster packs (usually two Dragons Exalted, one Emerging Powers and one Black & White) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Toyste Beach's art came to Japan in spring 2013 as an unnumbered promo at Battle Carnival 2013 Spring, a prize for collecting 10 PokéCard Points; players earned one for each event they entered at a venue.

A Rayquaza-EX from the Legendary EX Tins of 2012, out in some countries in August and in North America in September. Each tin held Mewtwo-EX BW45, Darkrai-EX BW46 or Rayquaza-EX, all three with new art, and four booster packs (usually two Dragons Exalted, one Emerging Powers and one Black & White) and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. Eske Yoshinob, who drew the Rayquaza-EX of Dragons Exalted, made new art for this card.

The art came to Japan in August 2013 as an unnumbered promo for the top four players of each league in the Mystery Card Battle at the Pokémon Game Show in Tokyo. Rayquaza-EX was given out only on the second day, 18 August, so just eight were handed out.

Altaria was the prerelease card of Dragons Exalted, given with a deck box at the set's prerelease tournaments in late July and early August 2012, and it carries the Dragons Exalted logo on the art, which shows the Pokémon League of Unova and N's Castle.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan in spring 2012 as Altaria 148/BW-P, given to those who bought a Garchomp or Hydreigon half deck at the Garchomp•Hydreigon Cup tournaments in April and at the Battle Carnival events of May and June. The English card credits HiRON, who drew the Altaria in the set; the Japanese promo credits 5ban Graphics. Staff at the prereleases got copies with STAFF printed on the art.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed in the corner of the art, for the staff of the Dragons Exalted prerelease tournaments.

A holofoil Lilligant from a Dragons Exalted blister of August 2012, with a Petilil from Emerging Powers, one Dragons Exalted booster pack, a sampling pack and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The other blister of that kind held the Excadrill line from Emerging Powers.

Naoki Saito's art first came in Japan in December 2011 as Lilligant 117/BW-P, in the Special Campaign Pack Zoroark, a blister with one booster pack each of Dark Rush, Hail Blizzard and Psycho Drive and a playmat.

Tropical Beach returned as the promo card of the 2012 Pokémon World Championships, held from 10 to 12 August 2012 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii. Competitors received the card in seven languages and staff got a Staff copy. 2012 was the first year with a Champion stamp above Finalist, so the trophy versions run from Top Thirty-Two up to Champion.

tell.text: "CHAMPION" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"QUARTER-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"SEMI-FINALIST" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
"STAFF" printed on the card, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: for the people who ran the event.

description.text: The stamped staff copy, given to those who helped run the 2012 World Championships. Other stamped copies went to the top players in each division.

"TOP THIRTY-TWO" printed below the card text, with the World Championships stamp on the picture: a prize for that placing.
A World Championships stamp on the picture: "Worlds" and the year on early cards, the World Championships logo and year on later ones.

description.text: The 2012 Tropical Beach, given to every player of the trading card game at the start of the 2012 World Championships, in a commemorative collection with the card in seven languages.

Crobat was the prerelease card of Plasma Storm, the set released in February 2013, and it carries the Plasma Storm logo on the art. Its blue frame and the Team Plasma emblem behind its text mark it as one of the set's Team Plasma cards.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan in 2012 as Crobat 181/BW-P, given to customers who bought a booster box of Plasma Gale, the Japanese set behind Plasma Storm. The set has its own Crobat with other art. Staff at the prereleases got copies with STAFF printed on the art.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed in the corner of the art, for the staff of the Plasma Storm prerelease tournaments.

A reverse holofoil Lillipup from the Emerging Challenges Box of September 2012, with one of four theme decks from Emerging Powers and Noble Victories, two booster packs, and reverse holofoil copies of Herdier and Stoutland from the Black & White set.

Mizue's art first came in Japan in 2011 in the Cobalion Battle Strength Deck. The other cards of that deck came to English in Emerging Powers in August 2011, a year earlier, without this Lillipup, and the promo still carries a 2011 copyright date.

Flygon was the prerelease card of Boundaries Crossed, given with a deck box at the set's prerelease tournaments on the weekends of 27 October and 3 November 2012, and it carries the Boundaries Crossed logo on the art.

BERUBURI's art first came in Japan in 2012 as Flygon 157/BW-P, given to customers who bought a booster box of Freeze Bolt or Cold Flare; the Japanese print carries those sets' logos. The set has its own Flygon with other art. Staff at the prereleases got copies with STAFF printed on the art.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed in the corner of the art, for the staff of the Boundaries Crossed prerelease tournaments.

A Pikachu from a Boundaries Crossed blister of November 2012, with a holofoil Raichu from Next Destinies, one Boundaries Crossed booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The other blister of that kind held Elgyem BW55. A cosmos holofoil copy came out only in Italy.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan in November 2011 as Pikachu 108/BW-P, packed with the Beginning Set Pikachu Version. A non-holo copy with a stamp, 163/BW-P, came with the Pokémon Card Game BW National Illustrated Encyclopedia in July 2012.

tell.text: Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.

description.text:
An Elgyem from a Boundaries Crossed blister of November 2012, with a holofoil Beheeyem from Next Destinies, one Boundaries Crossed booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The other blister of that kind held Pikachu BW54.

Mizue's art first came in Japan as Elgyem 126/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's March 2012 Gym Challenge tournaments, like Empoleon BW56; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo.

A holofoil Empoleon from the Boundaries Crossed three-pack blister of November 2012, with three Boundaries Crossed booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Haxorus BW57.

Shin Nagasawa's art, set on Twist Mountain, first came in Japan as Empoleon 125/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's March 2012 Gym Challenge tournaments, like Elgyem BW55; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo.

A holofoil Haxorus from the Boundaries Crossed three-pack blister of November 2012, with three Boundaries Crossed booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Empoleon BW56. Early store pictures of the Haxorus blister showed the Haxorus from Noble Victories instead of this card.

kawayoo's art first came in Japan in January 2012 as Haxorus 121/BW-P, packed with the Pokémon Card Game BW Battle & Win Book, a CoroCoro guidebook that also came with a Heavy Ball card.

A holofoil Black Kyurem from the Black Kyurem Box of April 2013, with a Black Kyurem figure, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The White Kyurem Box held White Kyurem BW59.

Shin Nagasawa drew new art for this reprint of the Black Kyurem from Boundaries Crossed (number 100, drawn by 5ban Graphics), which also came as a cracked ice holofoil in the Ice Shock theme deck. The two boxes were first announced for November 2012, to come out the same day as Boundaries Crossed, but distributors dropped them from their listings that September, and they reached stores in April 2013.

A holofoil White Kyurem from the White Kyurem Box of April 2013, with a White Kyurem figure, four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The Black Kyurem Box held Black Kyurem BW58.

Shin Nagasawa drew new art for this reprint of the White Kyurem from Boundaries Crossed (number 102, drawn by 5ban Graphics), which also came as a cracked ice holofoil in the Cold Fire theme deck. The two boxes were first announced for November 2012, to come out the same day as Boundaries Crossed, but distributors dropped them from their listings that September, and they reached stores in April 2013.

A holofoil Keldeo from the Keldeo Box of October 2012, the first English Keldeo card. The box held a figure of Keldeo in its Resolute Form, an oversized Keldeo-EX released before that card came out in Boundaries Crossed, and three Black & White Series booster packs, but no code card for the online game. A non-holo copy came with a DVD of the film Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice in 2013.

5ban Graphics' art, with Keldeo in its Ordinary Form, first came in Japan as Keldeo 162/BW-P. From 13 July 2012, the day Freeze Bolt and Cold Flare came out, stores gave it to customers who spent 1,000 yen on Pokémon card products, and Pokémon Centers gave a copy with their own stamp, 164/BW-P. In Korea the card marked the film's release in cinemas.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

distributions.name: Pokémon the Movie: Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice home video

description.text: A non-holo copy that came with a DVD of the film Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice in 2013.

tell.text: Holo foil of fine horizontal stripes.

description.text:
Keldeo-EX in its Resolute Form, from the EX Power Tins of March 2013. Each tin held one of three Pokémon-EX from Boundaries Crossed with new art (this card, Black Kyurem-EX BW62 or White Kyurem-EX BW63), one of two Meloetta cards (BW68 and BW69), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Toyste Beach, who drew the Keldeo-EX in Boundaries Crossed, drew this new art too. In Japan it became a prize at the Mystery Card Battle of the Pokémon Game Show in Tokyo: the top four players of each league received it on 17 August 2013, eight copies in all, and the next day's prize was Rayquaza-EX.

Black Kyurem-EX from the EX Power Tins of March 2013. Each tin held one of three Pokémon-EX from Boundaries Crossed with new art (this card, Keldeo-EX BW61 or White Kyurem-EX BW63), one of two Meloetta cards (BW68 and BW69), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Eske Yoshinob, who drew the Black Kyurem-EX in Boundaries Crossed, drew this new art too. The attack Freeze Shock takes its Japanese name from Freeze Bolt, the Japanese set where Black Kyurem-EX first appeared.

White Kyurem-EX from the EX Power Tins of March 2013. Each tin held one of three Pokémon-EX from Boundaries Crossed with new art (this card, Keldeo-EX BW61 or Black Kyurem-EX BW62), one of two Meloetta cards (BW68 and BW69), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Eske Yoshinob, who drew the White Kyurem-EX in Boundaries Crossed, drew this new art too. The attack Ice Burn takes its Japanese name from Cold Flare, the Japanese set where White Kyurem-EX first appeared.

A holofoil Drifblim from the Plasma Storm Stage 1 blister of February 2013, with Drifloon from Dragons Exalted, one Plasma Storm booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The other blister of that kind held Jigglypuff BW65. These copies use the pixel-pattern cosmos holofoil of the time; a later reissue, the Plasma Storm Rerelease Blister, has the card on the smoother cosmos holofoil of the XY series.

Naoki Saito's art, with the Unova Pokémon League behind Drifblim, first came in Japan as Drifblim 147/BW-P. It was given with a Garchomp or Hydreigon Half Deck to players at the Garchomp•Hydreigon Cup tournaments of April 2012, and again at the Battle Carnival Spring 2012 events of May and June. Dragons Exalted has its own Drifblim, drawn by Kanako Eo.

tell.text: Holo foil of dots and circles of different sizes, like a night sky.
Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.

description.text:
A Jigglypuff from the Plasma Storm Stage 1 blister of February 2013, with a cosmos holofoil Wigglytuff from Next Destinies made for the blister, one Plasma Storm booster pack and a sampling pack of three common cards. The other blister of that kind held Drifblim BW64.

MAHOU's art first came in Japan as Jigglypuff 127/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's March 2012 Gym Challenge tournaments; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo.

A holofoil Ninetales from the Plasma Storm three-pack blister of February 2013, with three Plasma Storm booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Ampharos BW67.

Hideaki Hakozaki redrew his Ninetales from Dragons Exalted for this card. It first came in Japan as Ninetales 123/BW-P, given to customers who bought a booster box of Dragon Blast or Dragon Blade, and the Japanese print carries those sets' logos.

Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.

description.text:
A holofoil Ampharos from the Plasma Storm three-pack blister of February 2013, with three Plasma Storm booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Ninetales BW66.

Naoki Saito's art, with Dragonspiral Tower behind Ampharos, first came in Japan as Ampharos 134/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's June 2012 Gym Challenge tournaments; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo. From the 2014-15 season no Mareep or Flaaffy card was left in the Modified format, so this Ampharos had nothing to evolve from there.

tell.text: Holo foil of dots and circles of different sizes, like a night sky.
Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.

description.text:
Meloetta in its Aria Forme, one of two non-holo Meloetta cards packed at random in the EX Power Tins of March 2013; the other is BW69. Each tin also held one of three Pokémon-EX with new art (BW61-BW63), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Naoki Saito's art first came in Japan as Meloetta 160/BW-P, one of Meloetta's first two cards, given with Happy Meals at McDonald's restaurants on 28 and 29 July 2012.

Meloetta in its Pirouette Forme, one of two non-holo Meloetta cards packed at random in the EX Power Tins of March 2013; the other is BW68. Each tin also held one of three Pokémon-EX with new art (BW61-BW63), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Shin Nagasawa's art first came in Japan as Meloetta 161/BW-P, one of Meloetta's first two cards, given with Happy Meals at McDonald's restaurants on 28 and 29 July 2012.

A cracked ice holofoil Virizion from the Legends of Justice Box of February 2013, which held Virizion (BW70), Terrakion (BW71) and Cobalion (BW72), the three Swords of Justice, as cracked ice holofoil cards with three Black & White Series booster packs.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Virizion 154/BW-P, in sets sold from 13 July 2012 to mark the film Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice, in which the three Swords of Justice appear.

A cracked ice holofoil Terrakion from the Legends of Justice Box of February 2013, which held Virizion (BW70), Terrakion (BW71) and Cobalion (BW72), the three Swords of Justice, as cracked ice holofoil cards with three Black & White Series booster packs.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Terrakion 155/BW-P, in sets sold from 13 July 2012 to mark the film Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice, in which the three Swords of Justice appear.

A cracked ice holofoil Cobalion from the Legends of Justice Box of February 2013, which held Virizion (BW70), Terrakion (BW71) and Cobalion (BW72), the three Swords of Justice, as cracked ice holofoil cards with three Black & White Series booster packs.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Cobalion 156/BW-P, in sets sold from 13 July 2012 to mark the film Kyurem vs. the Sword of Justice, in which the three Swords of Justice appear.

A full art Team Plasma Darkrai from the Team Plasma Box of May 2013, with Giratina BW74, a jumbo copy of this Darkrai, three Black & White Series booster packs and a Team Plasma coin.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan in the Team Plasma Battle Gift Set of November 2012. Darkrai and Giratina were the last of that set's cards to come out in English; the rest had come in Plasma Freeze. The attack Dark Hole takes its Japanese name from Dark Void, a move Darkrai learns in the games.

tell.text: The picture shines; the rest of the card doesn't.
An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.

description.text:
A full art Team Plasma Giratina from the Team Plasma Box of May 2013, with Darkrai BW73, a jumbo copy of that Darkrai, three Black & White Series booster packs and a Team Plasma coin.

5ban Graphics redrew the Giratina from Plasma Storm (number 62) as a full art card for Japan's Team Plasma Battle Gift Set of November 2012. Giratina and Darkrai were the last of that set's cards to come out in English; the rest had come in Plasma Freeze.

Metagross was the prerelease card of Plasma Freeze, given with a deck box at the set's prerelease tournaments in April 2013, and it carries the Plasma Freeze logo on the art.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan in December 2012 as Metagross 197/BW-P, given to customers who bought a booster box of Spiral Force or Thunder Knuckle; the Japanese print carries those sets' logos. Plasma Freeze has its own Metagross with other art. Staff at the prereleases got copies with STAFF printed in gold on the art.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed on the art, for the staff of the Plasma Freeze prerelease tournaments.

A Team Plasma Electrode from a Plasma Freeze single-pack blister of May 2013, with one Plasma Freeze booster pack and a code card for the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. The other blister of that kind held a cosmos holofoil Moltres from Next Destinies.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Electrode 173/BW-P, from the ten-card random packs of Japan's February 2013 Gym Challenge tournaments; the Japanese print carries the Gym Challenge logo.

A holofoil Team Plasma Landorus in its Therian Forme, from the Plasma Freeze three-pack blister of May 2013, with three Plasma Freeze booster packs and a Team Plasma coin. The other three-pack blister held Druddigon BW80. The card was meant for an English Landorus Box, sold in other languages but cancelled in English, and took the blister place planned for Pikachu BW77 and Raichu BW78.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Landorus 192/BW-P, given to players in the Victory Cup tournaments of Battle Carnival 2012 Autumn, held in Sapporo, Osaka and Tokyo in November 2012; the Japanese print carries the Battle Carnival logo. It is the only Fighting-type Team Plasma Pokémon.

A Team Plasma Druddigon in two foils. The cosmos holofoil copy came in the Plasma Freeze three-pack blister of May 2013, with three Plasma Freeze booster packs and a Team Plasma coin; the other three-pack blister held Landorus BW79. The tinsel holofoil copy came later in 2013 in the Deoxys Box, with a Deoxys figure, an oversized Deoxys-EX from Plasma Freeze and three Black & White Series booster packs. When a planned English Landorus Box was cancelled, a cosmos version of the Deoxys Box's Druddigon joined Landorus in the blisters, which is why the card exists in both foils.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Druddigon 201/BW-P, one of four cards that 7-Eleven stores gave at random from 25 December 2012 to customers who bought four booster packs of the latest sets.

tell.text: Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.
Holo foil of fine horizontal stripes.

description.text:
Thundurus-EX from the Team Plasma Tins of September 2013. Each tin held one of three Team Plasma Pokémon-EX with new art (this card, Deoxys-EX BW82 or Lugia-EX BW83), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card that unlocked the same card in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online. A European distributor had announced the three tins that April.

Eske Yoshinob, who drew the regular Thundurus-EX in Plasma Freeze, drew this new art too. The attack Raiden Knuckle takes its Japanese name from Thunder Knuckle, the Japanese set where Thundurus-EX first appeared.

Deoxys-EX from the Team Plasma Tins of September 2013. Each tin held one of three Team Plasma Pokémon-EX with new art (this card, Thundurus-EX BW81 or Lugia-EX BW83), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card that unlocked the same card in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Eske Yoshinob, who drew the regular Deoxys-EX in Plasma Freeze, drew this new art too. The attack Helix Force takes its Japanese name from Spiral Force, the Japanese set where Deoxys-EX first appeared.

Lugia-EX from the Team Plasma Tins of September 2013. Each tin held one of three Team Plasma Pokémon-EX with new art (this card, Thundurus-EX BW81 or Deoxys-EX BW82), four Black & White Series booster packs and a code card that unlocked the same card in the Pokémon Trading Card Game Online.

Toyste Beach, who drew both prints of Lugia-EX in Plasma Storm, drew this new art too. The attack Plasma Gale shares its name with the Japanese set where Lugia-EX first appeared.

Porygon-Z was the prerelease card of Plasma Blast, given at the prerelease tournaments held before the set came out on 14 August 2013, with the Plasma Blast logo on the art. A copy with STAFF printed on the art went to the staff of those events.

5ban Graphics drew this art for Porygon-Z 208/BW-P, which Japanese stores gave from March 2013 to customers who bought a booster box of Megalo Cannon; that print carries the Megalo Cannon logo instead. 5ban Graphics also drew the other art of the same card in Megalo Cannon, which became Plasma Blast's Porygon-Z (number 74).

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed on the art, for the staff of the Plasma Blast prerelease tournaments.

A holofoil Lucario from the Plasma Blast three-pack blister of August 2013, with three Plasma Blast booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Genesect BW86, and two single-pack blisters held cosmos holofoil copies of Blaziken and Krookodile from Dark Explorers.

Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan in February 2013 as Lucario 203/BW-P, one of five non-holo cards in special packs of Daiichi's melon bread and curry bread. The art shows Lostlorn Forest, recognizable by Zoroark's motorhome.

A holofoil Genesect from the Plasma Blast three-pack blister of August 2013, with three Plasma Blast booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Lucario BW85.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan as Genesect 219/BW-P, given from 20 April 2013 with purchases of Pokémon goods at selected stores, to mark the advance tickets for the film Genesect and the Legend Awakened (ExtremeSpeed Genesect: Mewtwo Awakens in Japan).

A holofoil Leafeon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Leafeon in Dark Explorers (number 6), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Leafeon 182/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Flareon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Flareon in Dark Explorers (number 12), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Flareon 183/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Vaporeon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Vaporeon in Dark Explorers (number 25), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Vaporeon 184/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Glaceon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Glaceon in Dark Explorers (number 30), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Glaceon 185/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Jolteon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Jolteon in Dark Explorers (number 37), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Jolteon 186/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Espeon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Espeon in Dark Explorers (number 48), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Espeon 187/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Umbreon from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The card has the attacks of the Umbreon in Dark Explorers (number 60), with new art by The Pokémon Company's art team. In Japan it was Umbreon 188/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign.

A holofoil Eevee from the Sylveon Collection of 15 November 2013, which brought Sylveon's first card, before even Japan had one, with a Sylveon figure, a Fairy Energy, four Black & White Series booster packs and holofoil promos of Eevee and its seven other evolutions of the time (BW87-BW94).

The Pokémon Company's art team drew this card for Japan's Eevee 189/BW-P, one of eight cards in a File Collection released on 23 November 2012 during the Pokémon Center's Eevee Collection campaign. When the card was printed again in the Japanese set Spiral Force, Naoki Saito drew new art for it, and that version is the Eevee in Plasma Freeze (number 89).

Champions Festival was the promo card of the 2013 Pokémon World Championships, the first card of that name, given out at the tournament held from 9 to 11 August 2013 at the Vancouver Convention Centre, the first World Championships outside the United States. Competitors received the card in seven languages, staff got a Staff copy, and the top finishers in each division got copies stamped with their placement, from Top Thirty-Two up to Champion. How many trophy copies were handed out changed from year to year.

description.text: The 2013 Champions Festival, given to every player of the trading card game at the start of the 2013 World Championships, in a nine-card binder: the card in seven languages, a card with the 2013 World Championships logo and an advertisement for the 2013 World Championship Decks.

Tornadus-EX was the prerelease card of Legendary Treasures, given at the set's prerelease tournaments, which began on 26 October 2013, with the Legendary Treasures logo on the art. A copy with STAFF printed on the art went to the staff of those events.

Ryo Ueda drew this art for Tornadus-EX 230/BW-P, which Japanese stores gave from 13 July 2013 to customers who bought a booster box of EX Battle Boost; that print carries the EX Battle Boost logo instead. The card is the Tornadus-EX of Dark Explorers (number 90), drawn there by Shizurow.

tell.text: The expansion's logo stamped in foil at the bottom right of the picture.
The Prerelease stamp plus the word "STAFF", for the people who ran the Prerelease events.

description.text: A copy with STAFF printed on the art, for the staff of the Legendary Treasures prerelease tournaments.

A holofoil Eevee from the Legendary Treasures three-pack blister of November 2013, with three Legendary Treasures booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Mew BW98. These blisters' promos were the first printed on a smoother style of cosmos holofoil, which replaced the earlier pixel-style pattern until 2023.

Akira Komayama's art, with Eevee in front of Pikachu, first came in Japan as Eevee 235/BW-P, the prize of a stamp rally at 7-Eleven stores for the Pokémon Fair 2013. Players who collected four different stamps of 24 at different stores received it, with stamps of Pokémon from that year's film from 15 to 31 July and of Legendary and Mythical Pokémon from 1 to 15 August.

A holofoil Mew from the Legendary Treasures three-pack blister of November 2013, with three Legendary Treasures booster packs and a coin. The other three-pack blister held Eevee BW97. These blisters' promos were the first printed on a smoother style of cosmos holofoil, which replaced the earlier pixel-style pattern until 2023.

Naoki Saito's art first came in Japan as Mew 220/BW-P, given to the players of the World Challenge Tournament at the spring 2013 Battle Carnival: in Fukuoka on 4 May, Nagoya on 12 May, Makuhari Messe in Chiba on 18 and 19 May and Osaka on 26 May. That print carries the Battle Carnival 2013 Spring logo on the art. The attack Psychic Exchange first appeared on Erika's Exeggutor in Gym Heroes.

A Genesect from the Red Genesect Collection of 25 September 2013, released ahead of the English film Genesect and the Legend Awakened. The collection held a 60-card deck built around the shiny red Genesect, a Red Genesect pin, a metallic Genesect coin, a deck box, damage counters, a playmat and two Black & White Series booster packs. The same card with other art, BW101, came with the film's DVD in December 2013.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan on 13 July 2013 as Genesect 231/BW-P, in the EX Battle Boost Campaign Pack, a blister of four EX Battle Boost booster packs released with that set, a Mewtwo vs Genesect deck kit and the film's Japanese premiere.

N, given out at Pokémon Leagues during the Fennekin season of the 2013-2014 league cycle, with the Pokémon League logo on the art. Two non-holo copies without the logo came in the Battle Arena Decks: Rayquaza vs. Keldeo of September 2016.

Yusuke Ohmura drew this art for N 180/BW-P, one of four cards Japanese stores gave to customers who spent 1,000 yen on Pokémon Card Game products when Plasma Gale came out; that print carries the Plasma Gale logo. A cracked ice reverse holofoil print of the same art, 218/BW-P, came in the Holo Card Special Pack N of 19 April 2013. N's first English card, drawn by Ken Sugimori, was in Noble Victories.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

A Genesect that came with the DVD of the film Genesect and the Legend Awakened, released on 3 December 2013. It is the same card as Genesect BW99 from the Red Genesect Collection, with other art.

5ban Graphics' art first came in Japan on 13 July 2013 as Genesect 232/BW-P, in the Movie Commemoration Genesect Set, a blister of two Megalo Cannon and two EX Battle Boost booster packs sold at cinemas showing the film, ExtremeSpeed Genesect: Mewtwo Awakens.
